I'm working out the pattern from the recovery log: exact values for shard_file_lost, and ranges for below_retention_floor with widths that vary by benchmark—0.04 for arc_lite, 0.02 for gsm_plus, checking code_ms next.

I also notice the sink-outage incidents both map to no_bundle, and I'm checking whether these ranges are always positioned entirely below the retention floor, since the archive can't contradict itself—every below-floor range seems to end just under its suite's floor value. This means the worst case is the range width intersected with whatever the floor bound already implies.

This confirms ranges are clipped right at the floor boundary, so worst-case residual width is just min(range width, archive width) — the intersection of the outcome range with the archive constraint. I should check whether these ranges snap to some consistent grid, since r00049 also seems to follow this pattern.

Checking suite widths in raw units: arc_lite is 0.04, gsm_plus normalizes to 0.02, code_ms to 0.025 — trying to find a common origin by converting raw width through the random-guess normalization, but the numbers don't line up to a single shared unit. It looks like each suite just has its own fixed empirical width rather than deriving from a common raw quantity, and I want to verify this holds consistently.

Now I'm checking which runs from the log actually need requests versus which already have known values — the recovery-related runs (r01415, r01682, r01973, r01974, r02049, r02083, r02387, r02606) and the candidates from the plans. For any run whose value is already pinned down (via eval or shard), the archive-only range width is just zero, so a further request adds nothing. I'm working through the INC4471 runs specifically to see which ones have shard values already fixed and which are still open.

For a shard_file_lost run, its row did reach the archive and got screened against the pass-rate floor in effect at its finish time before being lost, so I know its value cleared that floor even though the actual number is gone.

For below_retention_floor, the value must fall strictly below the floor at the check instant. But since the floor screen applies consistently to every archived row, any lost row I can't recover a value for is still bounded by whatever floor was active when it finished — except the INC4471/INC4530 runs, which never entered the archive at all, so no floor constraint applies to them.

Turning to the recovery calculation itself, for a run's own record I need its category-appropriate range: raw suites are bounded below by their random-guess baseline since the harness never emits scores below chance, while normalized suites bound at zero. For arc_lite with a 0.36 floor, that gives a below-floor range of roughly [0.25, 0.3599], and the residual is whichever is smaller between that range's width and the category's typical width.

I'm also checking whether the range width is truly fixed per suite or clipped by the archive's own bounds, and whether normalized suites might report ranges in raw units instead — need to verify across all the rows.

For the digest constraint, I'm working out that runs finishing on the same UTC day have their pass rates summed, so unknowns on a given day must sum to a fixed residual after subtracting known values. Each unknown lies in its own box, and I need to intersect that with the per-day sum constraint (values quantized to 0.0001) to bound the contrast between 'to' and 'from' groups, where each run contributes a coefficient of ±1/N depending on its group.

I'm reasoning this reduces to a per-day linear program: maximize a weighted sum subject to lower/upper bounds and a fixed total, which is solvable by a greedy fractional-knapsack approach—sorting by coefficient and filling values from their bounds until the total is met, with at most one variable landing on a fractional break point.

Since everything is expressed in multiples of 0.0001, that break value also lands exactly on a 0.0001 multiple, meaning the optimum is always integral in that sense—so the smallest interval containing all achievable values is just [min, max] from this greedy solution. Now I want to cross-check the run counts per day against the digest: 19 runs on 07-09, 10 on 07-11, 6 on 07-12, 5 on 07-13, plus 16 runs for the late INC4530 campaign—verifying these against what the 07-11 digest actually reports.

Looking at the 07-11 digest sum, it's 2.48 across 10 runs, giving an average of 0.248, which is below the 0.25 raw threshold, suggesting some of these runs are on normalized suites rather than raw ones. Now I'm working through how recovery requests interact with guaranteed interval width — runs with known values or no_bundle status don't add uncertainty, but shard_file_lost runs need me to compute the guaranteed width as the max over all digest-consistent values of the resulting sharp interval width.

For below_floor recovery, the outcome is a range of the correct width whose exact position within the valid bounds is unconstrained, so I need to think of a range outcome as valid whenever some consistent assignment places the true value inside it, and the worst-case width has to account for wherever that range gets placed relative to the archive's lower and upper bounds.

Whether the interpretation clips ranges to fit within the archive's bounds or requires strict containment matters only at the edges — if the archive is narrower than the target width, but the worst-case width-w interval that's fully inside the archive gives the same answer either way, so the two interpretations converge on the same worst case when such an interval exists.

For multiple runs, the outcome becomes a joint assignment across all runs' constraints — value-type runs fix exact values, range-type runs pin x_i within [a_i, a_i+w_i], and I need the worst-case difference between max and min contrast subject to all these simultaneously, which is a nonconvex optimization in general unless the structure is simple enough to check directly which runs actually appear in the queries.

cd /tmp/work && python3 -c "
from load import *
import json
from collections import defaultdict
ws=defaultdict(set)
for r in reclog:
    if r['outcome']=='range':
        ws[plan[r['run_id']]['suite']].add(round(float(r['returned_hi'])-float(r['returned_lo']),6))
        fl=floor_at(rt[r['run_id']]); s=plan[r['run_id']]['suite']
        lb=suites[s]['random_guess'] if suites[s]['scoring']=='raw' else 0
        assert float(r['returned_hi'])<=fl-0.0001+1e-9 and float(r['returned_lo'])>=lb-1e-9, r
print(dict(ws))
q=json.load(open('/app/queries.json'))
ids=set(x['run_id'] for x in q['recovery'])|set(x['run_id'] for x in q['values'])
for x in q['widths']: ids|=set(x['recover'])
for x in q['plans']: ids|=set(x['candidates'])
for rid in sorted(ids):
    p=plan[rid]; s=L[rid][0]
    print(rid, cat(rid), p['suite'],p['curriculum'],p['retrieval'],p['decoder'], s['worker'], s['started_at'], rt[rid], 'floor',floor_at(rt[rid]), ev.get(rid), shard.get(rid))
"
